newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR - A SOCCER CLOWN WITH WAR NIGHTMARES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR - A SOCCER CLOWN WITH WAR NIGHTMARES.

text.p: Zimbabwe-born goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar, who won five championships with Liverpool, often played the clown during games but never forgot the horrors of war he experienced as a teenage conscript.
At his peak Grobbelaar was the great eccentric of English soccer, renowned for his ice-cool temperament during big matches and for making athletic diving saves.
The keeper, who goes on trial here on Tuesday accused of match-fixing, was also capable of making horrendous unforced errors which cost his club dear in several important European cup competitions.
But there is no doubt Liverpool's brilliant record in the 1980s owed much to Grobbelaar, who is still capable of pulling off stunning saves.

Grobbelaar, now playing for second division Plymouth Argyle after a spell at premier league Southampton, has not let the trial affect his nerves and was due to turn out for Zimbabwe on Sunday in a World Cup qualifying game against Togo.
He has always been a soccer showman -- seemingly irrational, often acrobatic and occasionally impetuous.
Down the years, some marvelled, others cringed, at his juggling and gymnastic antics. He outraged the traditionalists and caused his defenders panic attacks by wandering upfield.

But behind the laughter lay the nightmare of his national service in the Rhodesian army, when as a 17-year-old he took part in the protracted conflict which ended with Zimbabwean independence in 1980.
"I saw my best friends killed in the bush and I killed people myself. I still have nightmares in which I hear the screams and see the frightened faces," he once wrote.
"If war teaches you anything it is an appreciation of being alive. I will never apologise for laughing at life and enjoying my soccer," he said.

The prematurely balding keeper has few peers in the flamboyance stakes. When obliged to wear a mask to protect a face injury two seasons ago when playing for Southampton, he typically chose one in the colours of the Zimbabwean flag.
During a 13-year career at Anfield, he won league championship medals in 1982, 1983, 1984, 1986 and 1988 and shared in League Cup success in 1982, 1983 and 1984.
Grobbelaar also collected English F.A. Cup medals in 1986 and 1989 and helped Liverpool to the European Cup in 1984.
Despite his eccentricities Grobbelaar had many admirers, including former England manager Bobby Robson.
"Had Bruce been English he would, without question, have won international honours during my time as England's manager," Robson was once quoted as saying.
"Bruce isn't simply an outstanding goalkeeper, blessed with incredible agility. He also gives his team an extra defender. He reads the game like an outfield player."
Grobbelaar signed for Liverpool for 250,000 pounds sterling in 1981 from Vancouver Whitecaps in Canada after starting his English career with lowly Crewe in 1979.
Bruce David Grobbelaar was born on October 6, 1957 in what was then Rhodesia. He is married with two young children.
